content.value:
Transcription of MS EAP729/1/2/660 in the Chinmaya International Foundation's
                    collection

This eText is transcribed from digital scans of an Original manuscript written
                    in Devanāgarī script.

A transcription from a scan of MS Chinmaya International Foundation (CIF)
                    EAP729/1/2/660.

A text on the Yoga philosophy. A Jain text
                    because it mentions śukladhyāna, the three jewels (jñānadarśanacaritra),
                    aṣṭakarma and pārśvaprabhu (= pārśvanātha). It teaches a system of aṣṭāṅgayoga
                    (saṃyama, niyama, karaṇa, prāṇāyāma, pratyahārā samādhir dhāraṇā and dhyāna.
                    Dhyāna seems higher than samādhi. However, there are references to the no-mind
                    state and laya (absorption) in Brahma.

The text may be any of the several works of this title mentioned in NCC 22,
                    pp. 80-81. It is not
Śubhacandra
's
Jñānārṇava

children.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Yogapradīpa</s> (Lamp of Yoga).

children.text: yāvan na grasyate rogair yāvan nābhyeti te jarā |
children.translated_text: As long as you are not seized by diseases, as long as old age does not overtake you,

children.text: yāvan na kṣīyate vāyus tāvat kalyāṇam ācara
children.translated_text: as long as the vital breath is not diminished, so long perform what is auspicious.
Where have I come from? Where shall I go? From where have I arrived just now?

children.text: ko bandhur mama kasyāham ity ātmānaṃ vicintayet
children.translated_text: Who is my kinsman? To whom do I belong? Thus one should reflect upon the Self.

children.text: puruṣās tīrtham icchanti kiṃ tirthaiḥ kleśakāraṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: People desire pilgrimage places — what use are pilgrimages that cause affliction?
The pilgrimage of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), situated within the body, is considered superior to all pilgrimages.

children.text: idaṃ tīrtham idaṃ tīrtham iti jñātvā bhramante ye |
children.translated_text: Those who wander about thinking 'this is a sacred place, this is a sacred place' —

children.text: jñānadhyānavihīnās te sati tīrthaṃ svam eva hi
children.translated_text: devoid of knowledge and meditation, the true pilgrimage for them is indeed their own Self.
Dwelling in the body, it consumes everything acquired since birth;

children.text: kenāpi dṛśyate naiva svātmāyaṃ paśyato haraḥ
children.translated_text: it is seen by no one — this Self, for one who sees it, is <s>Hara</s> (the Remover of all).

children.text: lokair vilokyate cauro gate svalpe 'pi vastuni |
children.translated_text: A thief is noticed by people even when a small thing is lost,

children.text: sarvasvaharam ātmānaṃ manāk paśyanti no jaḍāḥ
children.translated_text: but the dull-witted do not in the least perceive the Self, which steals everything.
Even through darkness, the one who has taken refuge in the fortress of the body,
the Self concealed by ignorance, should always be sought out by yogins.
pleased,
is here declared to be the path to a good destiny;
The Self itself, when well-

children.text: aprasannaḥ punar ayaṃ durgatiḥ syād asaṃśayam
children.translated_text: when displeased, this very Self becomes the cause of misfortune, without doubt.
Visiting pilgrimage after pilgrimage, desiring the sight of that one —
that deity cannot be seen.
yet dwelling right here in this body,
Wandering from place to place for the sake of seeing the divine,
those of ignorant understanding do not perceive the deity who dwells within the body.
Free from all material elements, of the nature of knowledge, the stainless one —
the Self itself, liberated from <s>karma</s>, should be meditated upon by those desiring <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
Immersed in the nectar of contentment, always equal toward enemy and friend,
beyond the knowledge of pleasure and pain, turned away from passion and aversion,
glorious like a mass of radiance, beneficent to the entire universe,
ever blissful and joyous, complete — the Self should be contemplated as the Lord.
Resembling pure crystal, adorned with the quality of omniscience,
endowed with the attributes of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) — the Self should be meditated upon by the wise.

children.text: ṣaṭcakravat tu pīṭhādi sarvaṃ tyaktā mumukṣubhiḥ | [tyaktvā?]
children.translated_text: The six <s>cakras</s>, <s>pīṭhas</s> (seats), and all the rest should be abandoned by seekers of liberation;
upon, in meditation free from form.
this Self alone should be meditated
Thus, through the yoga of practice, by this meditation, yogins
beholding it directly.
perceive the Self dwelling within the body as it truly is,
By whom the <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person), free from the <s>guṇas</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature), is not known —
by that person alone pilgrimages, sacrifices, and the like should be resorted to, not by yogins.

children.text: ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ na jalaṃ tīrtham ucyate |
children.translated_text: Self-knowledge is the supreme pilgrimage; water is not called a pilgrimage.

children.text: svātmajñānena yac chaucaṃ tac chaucaṃ paramaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The purity that comes from knowledge of one's own Self — that purity is considered the highest.
Self-knowledge is the supreme <s>dharma</s>, the chief of all righteous actions;

children.text: pradhānaṃ sarvavidvānāṃ prāpyate hy amṛtaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: it is foremost among all the learned, for through it the immortal nectar is attained.

children.text: tapobhir dustapais taptair vratais tais taiś ca puṣkaraiḥ |
children.translated_text: Even by those who have performed difficult austerities, and by various excellent vows —

children.text: ātmajñānaṃ vinā mokṣo na bhaved yogīnām api
children.translated_text: without self-knowledge, liberation is not possible, even for yogins.
Containing all <s>dharmas</s>, glorious, free from all distinctions of class —

children.text: ātmāyaṃ jñāyate tena tasya janma vidyate
children.translated_text: this Self is known by that one; for such a person, there is no further birth.
Having thus meditated upon one's own Self within one's body, free from the body,
one should meditate upon the Lord of gods, established in the supreme state, for the sake of liberation.

children.text: śaṅkaro vā jineśo vā yo yasyābhimataḥ sa

children.translated_text: ways,
<s>Śaṅkara</s> or <s>Jineśa</s> (Lord of the Jinas) — whichever is one's chosen deity, al-

children.text: eka eva prabhuḥ śānto nirvāṇastho vilokyate
children.translated_text: that one Lord alone, peaceful, established in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is beheld.
Lord of gods, humans, and demons, worshipped, beneficent to the worlds,
free from all faults — he is proclaimed the Lord of gods.
Beyond the path of merit and demerit, the destroyer of the vine of worldly existence,
unmanifest yet of manifest form, omniscient, the seer of all —
formless, without appearance, beyond phenomenal elaboration, stainless,
ever full of bliss, the divine one, perfected, awakened, free from affliction —
infinite, absolute, eternal, of the nature of space, everlasting,
the god of gods, the Self of the universe, all-pervading, ancient —
transcending all actions and limiting attributes, both with parts and without parts,

children.text: paramātmā paraṃ jyotiḥ paraṃ brahma parāt paraḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self), the supreme light, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, beyond the beyond —
free from the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), devoid of smell and touch,

children.text: achedyaś cāpy abhedyaś ca nirlepo nirmalaprabhuḥ
children.translated_text: unbreakable and indivisible, untainted, the pure Lord —
with qualities and without qualities, peaceful, the deliverer across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
difficult to perceive yet having attained perceptibility, of beautiful hue yet beyond all color —

children.text: eko 'py anekarūpaś ca sthūlasūkṣmo laghur guruḥ |
children.translated_text: though one, of many forms; gross and subtle, light and heavy;
is here described.
established in the state of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this Lord of gods

children.text: brāhmaṇair lakṣyate brahmā viṣṇuḥ pītāṃ varais tathā |
children.translated_text: By <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> he is perceived as <s>Brahmā</s>; by worshippers of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as <s>Viṣṇu</s> likewise;

children.text: rudras tapasvibhir dṛṣṭa eṣa eva nirañjanaḥ
children.translated_text: by ascetics he is seen as <s>Rudra</s> — this very one is the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>).

children.text: jinendro jalpyate jainair buddhaḥ kṛtvā sa saugataiḥ |
children.translated_text: By <s>Jainas</s> he is called <s>Jinendra</s>; by <s>Bauddhas</s> (Buddhists) he is made <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: kaulikaiḥ kola ākhyātaḥ sa evāyaṃ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: by <s>Kaulikas</s> (Tantric practitioners) he is called <s>Kula</s> — this very one is the Eternal.
Just as a crystal, when free from limiting adjuncts, assumes many colors,

children.text: sa tathā darśanaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ khyāta eko

children.translated_text: is known in many ways.
so too, through six philosophical systems, this one, though one,
Just as water assumes many colors due to differences in the ground it rests upon,
so too, due to differences of disposition, he is sung of in various forms.

children.text: bhāvabhedān na ma sthanti darśanāny ekavartmanā |
children.translated_text: Due to differences of disposition, the philosophical systems do not stand on a single path,

children.text: ekatrāpi sthitāḥ kārye pañcaite viṣayā yathā
children.translated_text: just as the five sense-objects, though established in one thing, serve different purposes.

children.text: niṣakalo nirmamaḥ śāntaḥ sarvajñaḥ sukhadaḥ prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Without parts, without possessiveness, peaceful, omniscient, bestower of happiness, the Lord —

children.text: sa eva bhagavān eko devo jñeyo nirañjanaḥ
children.translated_text: he alone, the blessed one, the one God, is to be known as <s>Nirañjana</s> (the Stainless).
Of the nature of space, Lord of the universe, beyond action, time, and qualities,
free from the creations of <s>saṃsāra</s>, distinct from all luminosity,
filled with absolute knowledge, abiding in absolute bliss,
is here described.
attainable only through pure meditation — this Lord of gods
Thus, endowed with infinite qualities, infinite, abounding in happiness,
one should meditate upon the Lord of gods, established in the state of liberation, beyond rebirth.
One should bathe the Lord with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-water of tranquility, devotion, and inner purity;

children.text: pūjayet taṃ tato yogī bhāvaṃ puṣpaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ
children.translated_text: then the yogin should worship him with the fragrant flowers of devotion.

children.text: bhaktisthale viśāle ca vaśyaṃ kṛtvā sthiraṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the vast ground of devotion, having made the mind steady and controlled,
placing therein the oil filled with the love of supreme bliss and nectar,
and lighting a brilliant row of lamps with the radiance of awakened knowledge,

children.text: uttārayet prabhoḥ puṇyam ārārtrikam iti kramāt
children.translated_text: one should perform the meritorious <s>ārātrika</s> (lamp-waving ceremony) for the Lord, in proper sequence.
Always, by this method, for the Lord of gods, the supreme Lord, I
should become a worshipper in spirit — thus one should contemplate.
One's own <s>haṃsa</s> (individual soul), the inner Self, of the nature of consciousness, into the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self)
one should unite with the supreme <s>Haṃsa</s>; thereby one attains the state of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Making the two into one, through auspicious meditation, the knower of yoga

children.text: paramātmasvarūpaṃ taṃ svam ātmā cainaṃ vicintayet
children.translated_text: should contemplate that form of the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) as one's own Self.
Having well obtained the sovereignty of bliss, the sun of absolute knowledge,
(Supreme Self), born having abandoned the ocean of worldly existence.
I am of the nature of the <s>Paramātman</s>
I am the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>) God, dwelling at the summit of all worlds —
thus one should always meditate, for it is the cause of the imperishable state.
When the Self, absorbed in meditation, beholds the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>) deity,
tears of bliss should flow and the hair should stand on end — this is the sign.

children.text: saṃyamo niyamaś caiva karaṇaṃ ca tṛtīyakaṃ |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃyama</s> (self-restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), and <s>karaṇa</s> (posture) as the third,
<s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal), <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) likewise,

children.text: dhyānaṃ cetīha yogasya jñeyam aṣṭāṅgakaṃ budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) — these should be known by the wise as the eight limbs of yoga;

children.text: pūrṇāṅgakriyamāṇas tu muktaye syād asau satām
children.translated_text: when practiced with all limbs complete, this yoga leads the virtuous to liberation.

children.text:
taddharmas tadvrataṃ
                        dhyānaṃ tat ta yo yoga eva saḥ | [tat tat ?]
children.translated_text: that is its <s>dharma</s>, that is its vow, that is its meditation, that austerity — that is yoga itself;
That is its <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sa eva hi padāroho na yatra kliśyate manaḥ
children.translated_text: that alone is the ascent to the supreme state, where the mind is not afflicted.
Free from conceptual construction and alternatives, devoid of causal reasoning,
engaged in <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the object of meditation, in a pure and steady place,

children.text: niyuñjita sadā cittaṃ sabhāve bhāvanāṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: one should always focus the mind; practice contemplation in the true nature of reality.

children.text: pade tatra gato yogī na punar janmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: The yogin who reaches that state does not return to the condition of rebirth.

children.text: jñeyaṃ sarvapadātītaṃ jñānaṃ ca mana ucyate |
children.translated_text: The knowable is said to be that which transcends all states; knowledge is called the mind.

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ samaṃ kuryān nānyo mokṣapathaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: One should make knowledge and the knowable equal — there is no other path to liberation.

children.text: bhruvopari mano nītvā tat paraṃ cāvalokyate |
children.translated_text: Having led the mind above the eyebrows, that supreme reality is perceived;

children.text: parāt parataraṃ tac ca ta chukṣmaṃ tan nirañjanaṃ

children.translated_text: that which is subtle?
that which is beyond the beyond, that which is subtle, that which is the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>),
through the latter
it is not found.
through the former path there is liberation;
Through the pathless path, in the state of <s>unmanī</s> (transcendence of mind), liberation arises, beyond all paths.
Through the abandonment of the delusion of worldly existence, consisting of the single essence of bliss,
established in the natural state — this is declared to be the path to liberation for the virtuous.
When the mind is free from the body, devoid of inhalation and exhalation,
and going, free from all activity,
beyond the path of coming
without support, without foundation, yet the support of all, of great arising,

children.text: parācinaṃ padaṃ jñeyaṃ yogibhis tan nirañjanaṃ
children.translated_text: that state beyond the senses is to be known by yogins as the stainless (<s>Nirañjana</s>).

children.text: pavano mriyate yatra mano yatra vilīyate |
children.translated_text: Where the breath dies and where the mind dissolves,
The innate state (<s>sahaja sthāna</s>) should be known; it is subtle, free from aging, and immortal,
The mind, freed from all activity, through constant practice of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: unmanībhāvam āyātaṃ labhate tat padaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: having attained the state of <s>unmanī</s> (beyond-mind), one gradually obtains that state.
Free from attachment to sense objects, the mind well-restrained in the heart,

children.text: yadā yāty unmatibhāvaṃ tadā tat paramaṃ padaṃ
children.translated_text: when it attains the state of <s>unmanī</s> (beyond-mind), then that is the supreme state.

children.text: dhyātṛ dhyāno bhayābhāvo dhyeyanaikyaṃ padā vrajet |
children.translated_text: When the distinction between the meditator and meditation vanishes, and unity with the object of meditation is reached,
that state of <s>samarasā</s> (equal essence) is considered <s>ekīkaraṇa</s> (unification).
Of subtle, formless, pure meditation, something further —

children.text: athātaḥ procyate tattvaṃ durjñeyaṃ mahatām api
children.translated_text: now the <s>tattva</s> (reality) is declared, which is difficult to know even for the great ones.
by some person —
A dream obtained at night by one who is asleep and mute,

children.text: na brūte sno pi mūkas tu tena svapno na budhyate
children.translated_text: even that mute one does not tell, and therefore the dream is not understood.
as seen by the wise —
That mute person, and what kind of night, and the dream

children.text: phalaṃ ca yādṛśaṃ tasya śṛṇu saumya tadā darāt
children.translated_text: and what fruit thereof — listen, O gentle one, to that carefully.

children.text: avidyā rātri supte na citta mūkena yoginā |
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) is the night; the sleeping mute one is the mind of the <s>yogī</s>;
the dream obtained is full of <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual feeling), and it bestows bliss upon him alone.

children.text: kṛtas tena sthiro bhāva parabrahmaṇi yoginā |
children.translated_text: By that <s>yogī</s>, a steady <s>bhāva</s> (contemplation) is established in <s>Parabrahman</s> (the Supreme Absolute);
the <s>bhāva</s> that has reached <s>Parabrahman</s> bears the fruit of liberation for him.
Beyond the duality of <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun), devoid of the movement of <s>vāyu</s> (breath),
the mind free from <s>saṅkalpa</s> (volition) is said to be in <s>Parabrahman</s>.
That <s>Parabrahman</s> itself should be known; for the sake of <s>siddhi</s> (perfection), by the wise,

children.text: sadā svapnārthaḥ kathitaḥ prājñaḥ yogayuktyā tavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: the meaning of the dream has always been told — the wise one, through the method of <s>yoga</s>, is now before you.

children.text: na kiṃ cic cintayec cittam unmanībhāvasaṅgataṃ |
children.translated_text: The mind should not think of anything, being absorbed in the state of <s>unmanī</s> (beyond-mind);
formless, supremely subtle — that is called the great <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).
The distinctions of <s>śukladhyāna</s> (pure meditation) through bodily forms and words that were previously
in a palace.
described were for the sake of its growth, like steps

children.text: smi kva gantāsmi kiṃ karomi smarāmi kiṃ |
children.translated_text: Where shall I go? What shall I do? What do I remember?"
"What am I?

children.text: iti yogī na jānāti laye līno nirañjane
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>yogī</s> does not know, absorbed in <s>laya</s> (dissolution), merged in the stainless.
With the eye of knowledge veiled by sense objects like a covering,
beings do not see <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), which is the gateway to the city of <s>siddhi</s> (perfection).
By the five restless senses, each with its own name of a sense object,

children.text: aniruddhair indriyād vai dhyānād avyāvartate manaḥ
children.translated_text: being unrestrained, the mind is indeed turned away from <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

children.text: śamaṃ nīteṣu teṣv atra kaṣāyeṣv indriyeṣv api |
children.translated_text: When those impurities of the senses are brought to calm,
the mind, made steady through meditation, should be rendered free from <s>saṅkalpa</s> (volition).
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is endowed with mind, and the mind therein is restless and unsteady;

children.text: vaśyaṃ yena kṛtaṃ tasya bhaved vaśyaṃ jagatrayaṃ
children.translated_text: he by whom it is controlled — for him the three worlds become subject.

children.text: yac chubhaṃ karmakatṛtvaṃ tat kuryān manasā saha |
children.translated_text: Whatever auspicious action one performs, one should do it together with the mind;

children.text: manas tulyaṃ phalaṃ yasmāt śūnye śūnyaṃ bhavet punaḥ
children.translated_text: since the fruit is equal to the mind — in emptiness, it becomes empty again.

children.text: kṛtvābhyāso yathā dhanvī lakṣyaṃ vidhyati tanmanā |
children.translated_text: Just as an archer, having practiced, hits the target with focused mind,
accomplishes the desired action.
so too the <s>yogī</s>, with one-pointed mind,

children.text: tasmād apy uttamaṃ sāraṃ pavitraṃ karmanāśanaṃ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind should be made even more excellent, pure, and capable of destroying <s>karma</s>,
supreme among all <s>dharmas</s> (duties), established in <s>śamarasa</s> (the essence of tranquility).

children.text: janma lakṣyair vratair ugrair yatraiva kṣīyate kva cit |
children.translated_text: Where <s>karma</s> accumulated over births is exhausted through fierce vows,

children.text: manaḥ śamarase magnaṃ tat karma kṣayayet kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: the mind immersed in <s>śamarasa</s> (tranquil essence) can destroy that <s>karma</s> in an instant.
Through the renunciation of all undertakings, when the mind has attained <s>śamarasa</s> (tranquil essence),

children.text: sā siddhiḥ syāt satāṃ yāno sarvatīrthāvagāhane
children.translated_text: that <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) becomes the path of the virtuous, equal to bathing in all <s>tīrthas</s> (holy places).
While the supreme <s>yoga</s> of <s>samarasātmaka</s> (equal essence) is available, the deluded ones,

children.text: yogaṃ yogaṃ prakurvāṇā saṃbhrāmanti diśo diśo
children.translated_text: practicing this yoga and that yoga, wander about in all directions.
only as long as one does not find <s>Brahman</s>;
The distinction of <s>varṇa</s> (caste) exists

children.text: saṃprāptā paramaṃ brahma sarve varṇā dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: having attained the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, all <s>varṇas</s> become twice-born.
The paths of <s>dharma</s> are many, with divisions among the <s>darśanas</s> (philosophical systems);

children.text: mokṣārthaṃ samatāṃ yāti samudraṃ sarito yathā

children.translated_text: Do they go?
for the sake of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), they reach equality, just as rivers reach the ocean.
Just as the milk of cows of many colors is of one color,
so the path of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) of the six <s>darśanas</s> (philosophical systems) is the same.
Free from the fabrications of <s>saṅkalpa</s> (volition), devoid of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion),
absorbed in eternal bliss and <s>laya</s> (dissolution) — such a mind is called <s>samarasa</s> (of equal essence).

children.text: atītaṃ ca bhaviṣyac ca yan na śocati mānasaṃ |
children.translated_text: The mind that does not grieve over the past nor the future —
that is called <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity), like a lamp in a windless place.
Unattached, without appearance, formless, without support,
free from merit and sin — such a mind is regarded as <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimous).

children.text: gate śoko na yasyāstī na ca harṣaḥ samāgate |
children.translated_text: One who has no sorrow at loss, nor joy at gain,
whose mind is equal toward enemy and friend — that is called <s>sāmāyika</s> (equanimity) here.
scriptures composed by poor poets —
That which spreads in this world,
that is declared to be <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the cause of confusion about <s>samatā</s> (equality).

children.text: yathā rātrau tame mūḍhā naiva paśyanti jantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as at night in darkness, deluded beings do not see,
so too they do not perceive the <s>tattva</s> (reality), enveloped by the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
Wicked, made of delusion and <s>māyā</s> (illusion), for seekers of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) among the virtuous,
the bolt on the door of the path to liberation, created in the world.
<s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is eternally

children.text: iti jñātvā budhair nityaṃ svātmane hitavāñchayā |
children.translated_text: Knowing this, the wise, always with the desire for benefit to their own self,
<s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) created in the world —

children.text: iti jñātvā budhair nityaṃ dūratas tyājyā na śrotavyā kadā cana
children.translated_text: knowing this, the wise should always abandon it from afar and never listen to it.

children.text: [avidyā nirmitā tyājyā na śrotavyā kadā cana ?]

children.translated_text: The true knowledge spoken by the omniscient is the cause of severing worldly existence;
that alone should always be cultivated by the virtuous, as it bestows the path to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
<s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these are the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) within the body;

children.text: rajas tamaś ca santyajya sattvam ekaṃ samāśrayet
children.translated_text: abandoning <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, one should take refuge in <s>sattva</s> alone.
<s>Sattva</s> is the basis of all virtues; <s>sattva</s> upholds <s>dharma</s>;
<s>sattva</s> destroys <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence); <s>sattva</s> grants heaven and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
In that which is without support, formless, ever blissful, motionless, and auspicious,

children.text: santāṃ dhyānamaye saudhe sattvastambho dṛdho mataḥ
children.translated_text: in the palace of meditation of the saints, the pillar of <s>sattva</s> is considered firm.
Just as even a small spark of fire burns heaps of wood,
of <s>yogīs</s>, likewise.
so by <s>śukladhyāna</s> (pure meditation), the <s>karmas</s> (actions) are destroyed
The supreme <s>yogī</s> who always bathes in the great, pure water of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) —

children.text: lakṣam ekaṃ kathaṃ tiṣṭhet tasmin karma rajo malaḥ
children.translated_text: how can even a trace of <s>karma</s> (action), impurity, or <s>rajas</s> (passion) remain in him?

children.text: na laget padmini patre yathā toyaṃ svabhāvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as water does not cling to a lotus leaf by its very nature,
just as a stone placed in water is not split,

children.text: sphaṭiko malino na syāt rajasā chādito yathā |
children.translated_text: just as a crystal does not become impure, though covered by dust,

children.text: na lipyate tathā pāpair ātmā saddhyānam āśritaḥ
children.translated_text: so too the <s>ātman</s> (self), established in true meditation, is not tainted by sins.
Through <s>yoga</s> equal to <s>śukladhyāna</s> (pure meditation), the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is established in <s>Brahman</s>;
the <s>yogī</s> may enjoy the supreme fruit at the top of the branch.
even while standing on the ground,
Through this meditation on the supreme bliss of liberation, for the <s>yogīs</s>,

children.text: rūpātītaṃ nirākāraṃ dhyānaṃ dhyeyaṃ tato niśaṃ
children.translated_text: meditation that is beyond form and formless should be contemplated constantly.

children.text: granthānn abhyasya tattvārthaṃ tattvajñāne punaḥ sudhīḥ |
children.translated_text: Having studied the texts and understood the meaning of <s>tattva</s> (reality), the wise one, for the sake of <s>tattva-jñāna</s> (knowledge of reality),

children.text: palālam iva dhyānārthaṃ tyajed granthān śeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: should then abandon the texts, like chaff, for the sake of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation).

children.text: kṣīyante yāni kālena kiṃ taiḥ kartavyam akṣaraiḥ |
children.translated_text: What use are those perishable syllables that decay with time?

children.text: yāvan no nakṣaraprāptaṃ tāvan mokṣasukhaṃ kutaḥ
children.translated_text: Until the imperishable is attained, whence can there be the bliss of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)?
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is a wish-fulfilling tree in the world, blossoming with the flowers of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
bestowing happiness.
always bearing fruit with the immortal fruits of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),
Therefore act in such a way that, having taken shelter of the tree of <s>śukladhyāna</s> (pure meditation),
gathering the flowers of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), the wise one may obtain the fruit of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: asminn eva bhave saumya vyomarūpaḥ sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this very life, O gentle one, eternal, having the form of space,
through <s>śukladhyāna</s> (pure meditation), the ever-blissful <s>yogī</s> reaches the state of <s>mukti</s> (liberation).
Consisting of the triad of jewels — <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>darśana</s> (vision), and <s>cāritra</s> (conduct) —
<s>yoga</s> is proclaimed as the means for attaining the state of <s>mukti</s> (liberation).
That <s>yoga</s> which severs <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) through cessation of activity is the bestower of <s>mukti</s> (liberation);
it is again eightfold.
divided into limbs beginning with <s>saṃyama</s> (restraint),
<s>Soma</s> (moon), <s>Sūrya</s> (sun), and others too,
Gems, fire, stars,
illuminate only a small, external, earthly domain.
But the light arising from the innate <s>laya</s> (dissolution) illuminates within,
always revealing all three worlds in both their subtle and gross aspects.
is supreme;
The subtle object of supreme bliss and stillness, beyond one's own experience,
below the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above the head), one should meditate on the <s>anāhata nāda</s> (unstruck sound).
Like an unbroken stream of oil, like the resonance of a long bell,

children.text: layaṃ praṇavanādasya yas taṃ vetti sa yogavit
children.translated_text: he who knows the dissolution of the <s>praṇava nāda</s> (the sound of Oṃ) — he is a knower of <s>yoga</s>.

children.text: ghaṇṭānāde yathā prāpte praśāmyan madhuro bhavet |
children.translated_text: Just as when a bell's sound fades, a sweet, subsiding tone remains,
sound
should likewise be contemplated as peaceful.
so too the <s>anāhata</s> (unstruck)
It sounds in an unmanifest form, dwelling in the hearts of all beings;
<s>anāhata</s> (unstruck), therefore the sound is not of manifest origin.
that <s>nāda</s> (sound) is
That <s>nāda</s> (sound), pervading the entire body, is established at the tip of the nose;
perceptible to all beings, yet it is not truly seen — only aimed at.
Free from the sound of syllables, waveless, established in evenness —

children.text: yac cittaṃ sahajāvasthaṃ sa nādas tena bhidyate
children.translated_text: when the mind is in its innate state (<s>sahajāvasthā</s>), that <s>nāda</s> (sound) is thereby pierced.

children.text: tāvad eveṅdriyāṇi syuḥ kaṣāyās tāvad eva hi |
children.translated_text: The senses persist, and the afflictions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) persist just as long,

children.text: anāhate mano nāde yāval līnaṃ na yoginaḥ
children.translated_text: as the yogin's mind has not become absorbed in the <s>anāhata</s> (unstruck) sound.
Sensory pleasure appears so delightful only
is not obtained.
until the happiness born of absorption in the <s>anāhata</s>
The <s>karma</s> acquired from birth onward — by this meditation, for the yogin,

children.text: tamaḥ sūryodayeneva tat sarvaṃ naśyati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: all that is destroyed in an instant, as darkness by the rising sun.

children.text: sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca sākāraṃ śubhadhyānam iti sphutaṃ |
children.translated_text: Gross, subtle, and with form — this is clearly called auspicious meditation (<s>śubhadhyāna</s>).
That which transcends form is declared and called formless (<s>nirākāra</s>).
Formless meditation too, which transcends form and is resplendent,
is declared to be twofold, through the distinction of gross and subtle.

children.text: śarīraṃ sakalaṃ tyaktvā brahmadvāre sthiraṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Abandoning the entire body, making the mind steady at the <s>brahmadvāra</s> (door of <s>Brahman</s>) —

children.text: kriyate yadi tat sukṣmaṃ nirākāram ihocyate
children.translated_text: if this is done, that is called the subtle formless [meditation] here.
Through constant practice of pure meditation on the <s>anāhata</s> [sound],
one should direct the mind to yoga in the formless [state] at the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (twelve-finger space above the head).
The yogin, having abandoned the inner <s>Brahma</s>[-realm] and the self as agent,
should resort to the <s>brahmadvāra</s>, the formless, the abode of the Supreme Self.
The measure of one finger's breadth, perfectly round, resembling space —
the lord of yogins should first contemplate the <s>dvādaśānta</s> thus.
it is called the twelvefold Self (<s>dvādaśātman</s>).
[An auspicious sign appears to] the eye —

children.text: tasmād apy ūrdhvagaṃ brahma dvādaśānte tathā smṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: Beyond that too, <s>Brahman</s> ascending upward is thus remembered at the <s>dvādaśānta</s>.
Transcending <s>nāda</s> (sound), <s>bindu</s> (point), and <s>kalā</s> (phase), endowed with the phase of the Supreme Self —
one should always meditate on the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, the sole abode of eternal bliss.
restraining his own exceedingly restless senses,
The yogin, having checked the flow of afflictions (<s>kaṣāya</s>),

children.text: tyaktvā vā saṅgam anyaṃ paramapadasukhaprāptaye baddhabuddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: and abandoning other attachments, with intellect fixed on attaining the happiness of the supreme state,

children.text: kṛtvā cittaṃ sthiraṃ svaṃ śamarasakalitaṃ sattvaṃ ālambya bāḍhaṃ
children.translated_text: making his own mind steady, imbued with the essence of tranquility, firmly grasping <s>sattva</s>,

children.text: dhyānaṃ dhyātuṃ yateta pratidinam amalaṃ śuddhadharmāvitaṇḍaḥ
children.translated_text: should strive to meditate daily on pure meditation, free from disputatious doctrine.

children.text: chitvā saṃsṛtipāśam antarabalaṃ jitvātha mohādikaṃ dīkṣāṃ
children.translated_text: Having cut the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>, having conquered the inner forces [of delusion] and <s>moha</s> (delusion) and the like,

children.text: mokṣakarīṃ prapadya sa budhaḥ pārśvaprabhor udyataḥ |
children.translated_text: having undertaken the initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) that leads to liberation, that wise one, striving by the grace of the Lord,

children.text: brahmajñānalayena kevalamayaṃ jñānaṃ samutpādya ca prāyan
children.translated_text: having produced pure knowledge through absorption in the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>,
attains the state of liberation, always blissful, through the exhaustion of the eight <s>karmas</s>.
Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>), truth (<s>satya</s>), non-stealing (<s>asteya</s>), celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), non-attachment (<s>asaṅga</s>) —
is remembered as fivefold.
these are the vows herein; restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>)

children.text: śaucaṃ tapaś ca santoṣaḥ svādhyāyo devatāsmṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Purity (<s>śauca</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), contentment (<s>santoṣa</s>), self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), and remembrance of the deity —

children.text: niyamaḥ pañcadhā jñeyaḥ karaṇaṃ punar āsanaṃ
children.translated_text: the observances (<s>niyama</s>) are to be known as fivefold; the [third] practice is posture (<s>āsana</s>).
Steadiness in inhalation and exhalation constitutes <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control);
<s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) is the composed destruction of the sense-objects for the senses.
<s>Samādhi</s> is [the state where] worldly existence [becomes like] a blade of grass; contemplation of the meaning of [sacred] words;
for the sake of steadiness, <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is to be practiced by people — thus it is the means of [inner] wealth.

children.text: sthūle vā yadi vā sūkṣme sākāre ca nirākṛtau |
children.translated_text: Whether on the gross or the subtle, whether with form or formless,
one should meditate with a steady mind, meditation united with a single focused thought.

children.text: evaṃ yogo bhaved yogair aṣṭadhā saṃyamādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus yoga is accomplished by yogins through the eightfold [practice] beginning with restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>).
Meditation endowed with all excellences is the cause of well-being.

children.text: divi bhūmau tathā kāśe bahir antaś ca yo vibhūḥ |
children.translated_text: In heaven, on earth, and in space, outside and within, the all-pervading one —

children.text: yo vibhāty eva bhāsātmā tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ
children.translated_text: He who shines, the self-luminous Self — salutation to that All-Self!

children.text: nāhaṃ baddho vimuktaś ca iti yasyāsti niścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am neither bound nor liberated' — one who has this conviction,
is [truly] qualified
for this scripture.
no other person wiser than that — such a 'fool'
Having renounced all intentions, dwelling solely in solitary wealth [of the Self],
of the nature of the thought of nothingness — that is <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme state.
<s>Yogapradīpa</s>
is complete.
Thus the blessed
belongs to <s>Harilalya</s>.
